adapters.statement: The fixed graph with adjacency SHA256 3f910d235e38191b5ac47523c22166f1abfc4d1f3ad285b60d4c684392a6670d is a 99-vertex simple 14-regular graph in which every adjacent pair has exactly one common neighbor. Its complete 99-by-231 vertex-by-triangle incidence matrix has row weights 7, column weights 3, rank 98 over GF(3), and complete left kernel equal to the span of the constant vector. It fails the SRG99 integer identity at 5500 ordered entries and has unordered nonedge residual energy 5476. It is a counterexample only to an assertion that these incidence and adjacent-pair conditions alone force a nonconstant ternary left-kernel vector.

adapters.statement: For every 99-by-99 symmetric binary zero-diagonal matrix A with exact integer row degree14, put r_uv=(A^2)_uv+A_uv-2 for u<v, F3=sum_[u<v] 1[3 does not divide r_uv] and E=sum_[u<v] r_uv^2. Then F3<=E<=28*F3. If q_i counts these unordered residuals congruent to i modulo3, q1-q2 is divisible by3; the same congruence holds in every complete vertex row. Consequently F3=1 is impossible and F3=2 implies q1=q2=1. No existence or realization of these small defects is asserted.
